question: Should OpenClaw permanently support repeatable ordered configuration documents with first-owner-wins authority and an immutable Gateway startup snapshot?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but it establishes a new public configuration and operator-lifecycle contract whose ownership and long-term compatibility require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor bounded core contract
options.body: Approve the generic startup-only CLI seam, retain role-neutral IDs and path-scoped write blocking, then require a current-main rebase and full validation.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Decline the core contract and require managed hosts to materialize one canonical document before launching OpenClaw.

options.title: Narrow through the RFC
options.body: Pause this PR until the RFC defines a smaller validation or provenance API that managed hosts can build upon.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the generic startup-only CLI seam, retain role-neutral IDs and path-scoped write blocking, then require a current-main rebase and full validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects this person to configuration persistence, Gateway lifecycle, and compatibility-sensitive configuration behavior.
